What it means: Student marital status.
Why it may matter (not causal): May reflect different life responsibilities; non-actionable and not causal.

What it means: Admission pathway/mode used to enter the institution.
Why it may matter (not causal): Can capture different entry pathways, transfers, mature-entry routes, and prior education routes.

What it means: Position of this degree/program in the student's application preferences.
Encoding / unit: 0 = first choice; up to 9 = later choice
Why it may matter (not causal): Later preferences may correlate with program fit, but this is only an association.

What it means: Degree/program in which the student is enrolled.
Why it may matter (not causal): Programs can differ in workload, curriculum, selectivity, and historical retention patterns.

What it means: Whether the student follows a daytime or evening schedule.
Why it may matter (not causal): Schedule can relate to work/life constraints. This is NOT attendance percentage.

What it means: Qualification held before higher-education entry.
Why it may matter (not causal): Prior pathway can reflect preparation and transition into higher education.

What it means: Grade achieved in the previous qualification.
Why it may matter (not causal): Higher prior achievement may indicate stronger preparation.

What it means: Student nationality; the source column is misspelled as 'Nacionality'.
Why it may matter (not causal): Sensitive/non-actionable background variable; fairness should be checked.

What it means: Mother's education level.
Why it may matter (not causal): Family/socioeconomic-background proxy; non-actionable and not causal.

What it means: Father's education level.
Why it may matter (not causal): Family/socioeconomic-background proxy; non-actionable and not causal.

What it means: Mother's occupation category.
Why it may matter (not causal): Socioeconomic-context proxy; non-actionable and should be interpreted cautiously.

What it means: Father's occupation category.
Why it may matter (not causal): Socioeconomic-context proxy; non-actionable and should be interpreted cautiously.

What it means: Student admission grade.
Why it may matter (not causal): Direct indicator of academic preparation at entry.

What it means: Whether the student is classified as displaced.
Why it may matter (not causal): Relocation/living-context disruption may relate to support needs.

What it means: Whether the student has special educational needs.
Why it may matter (not causal): May indicate need for accessibility/support services; should never be framed as a deficit.

What it means: Whether the student has debtor status.
Why it may matter (not causal): May reflect financial/administrative pressure and is potentially actionable through support.

What it means: Whether tuition fees are up to date.
Why it may matter (not causal): Financial/administrative status can be a warning signal and is actionable through support.

What it means: Student gender as encoded by the source.
Why it may matter (not causal): Sensitive/non-actionable; model behavior across groups should be audited.

What it means: Whether the student has a scholarship.
Why it may matter (not causal): Can reflect access to financial support/resources.

What it means: Student age when enrolled.
Why it may matter (not causal): May correlate with work/family responsibilities and life stage; non-causal.

What it means: Whether the student is an international student.
Why it may matter (not causal): Can relate to adjustment/support context; sensitive/non-actionable as a reason.

What it means: Number of curricular units credited in Semester 1.
Why it may matter (not causal): Reflects recognized prior learning/credits and academic structure.

What it means: Number of units enrolled in Semester 1.
Why it may matter (not causal): Represents academic load.

What it means: Number of evaluations linked to Semester-1 curricular units.
Why it may matter (not causal): Reflects assessment activity and workload.

What it means: Number of Semester-1 curricular units passed/approved.
Why it may matter (not causal): Direct measure of early academic progress; expected to be highly informative.

What it means: Average grade in Semester 1.
Why it may matter (not causal): Direct measure of early academic achievement.

What it means: Number of Semester-1 units without evaluation.
Why it may matter (not causal): Can indicate incomplete/missed assessment activity or unusual progression.

What it means: Number of curricular units credited in Semester 2.
Why it may matter (not causal): Potentially predictive but future information at our Semester-1 warning point; excluded.

What it means: Number of units enrolled in Semester 2.
Why it may matter (not causal): Future information for the chosen early-warning point; excluded.

What it means: Number of Semester-2 evaluations.
Why it may matter (not causal): Future information for the chosen early-warning point; excluded.

What it means: Number of Semester-2 units passed/approved.
Why it may matter (not causal): Highly informative retrospectively, but too late for our Semester-1 intervention point; excluded.

What it means: Average grade in Semester 2.
Why it may matter (not causal): Highly informative but future information at the selected prediction point; excluded.

What it means: Number of Semester-2 units without evaluation.
Why it may matter (not causal): Future information for our operational prediction point; excluded.

What it means: Macroeconomic unemployment rate associated with the cohort.
Why it may matter (not causal): Economic-context variable; not directly actionable by the university.

What it means: Macroeconomic inflation rate associated with the cohort.
Why it may matter (not causal): Economic-context / possible financial-pressure proxy.

What it means: GDP macroeconomic indicator supplied with the dataset.
Encoding / unit: Unit not specified by source variable table
Why it may matter (not causal): Cohort-level economic context; not an individual cause.

What it means: Final status at the end of the normal duration of the course.
Why it may matter (not causal): Prediction outcome. Enrolled is unresolved and not treated as a confirmed negative label.
